reason: Recommend testing `k_loop_schedule` as fixed-base indexed loads in `Llibxsmm_478` and `Llibxsmm_70c`: remove the two per-step pointer increments, retain the four ordered FP32 FMOPA operations, then advance each base by its full span before the existing rewinds. This is distinct from the measured loop schedules, but indexed address generation may cost more than the increments it removes. Rank prefetch and panel packing first as bounded, distinct tests; neither has evidence of a likely win. The address-generation proposal is close to a previously measured pointer-end change. `cache_blocking` describes a two-K loop body that conflicts with the supplied current one-K source and overlaps prior two-step work, so it needs source clarification. The remaining proposals have limited relevance to n=512 or substantial rewrite and correctness risk. Historical scores show no promoted candidate or result above 1800 GFLOP/s; they do not establish causes.
